title: Algorithms, complexity & data structures
summary: Estimate how work grows before trying to make it faster with hardware.
html:
Estimate how work grows before trying to make it faster with hardware.

How the pieces connect

Define input scale → Choose representation → Find dependencies → Measure reality. Each transition is a place where an assumption can be inspected before the next layer of the system compounds it.

Count growth, then constants

Big-O describes an asymptotic upper bound, not a measured runtime. Scanning n records is O(n); comparison sorting is typically O(n log n); forming all pairwise similarities is O(n²). Constant factors, memory locality, and parallelism determine actual performance at a particular size.

Choose the representation

Arrays provide compact indexed storage. Hash tables give expected constant-time lookup under suitable assumptions. Trees organize ordered searches. Graphs represent relationships; adjacency lists are efficient for sparse edges, while dense matrices can be convenient for highly connected structures.

Dependencies control parallelism

Independent outputs can run concurrently. A reduction, such as summing a million values, needs a combination step but can use a logarithmic-depth tree. A recurrence that requires the previous state creates a sequential dependency. Concurrency describes overlapping progress; parallelism describes simultaneous execution.

Time-space tradeoffs

Caching spends memory to avoid repeated computation. Recomputing activations saves training memory but increases work. Tiling moves small reusable chunks into fast storage. Approximate nearest-neighbor indexes trade exact retrieval guarantees for speed and memory efficiency. Always state which resource the optimization spends.

Worked example

Doubling sequence length makes a dense attention score matrix four times larger: 4,096² becomes 8,192². At two bytes per element, a single unbatched, single-head score matrix grows from 32 MiB to 128 MiB. Memory-efficient attention changes materialization, while exact dense attention still involves quadratic pair interactions.

What goes wrong

An O(n) algorithm is not always faster than an O(n log n) one at small n. Benchmark representative sizes and include preprocessing, transfers, and allocations.

Check your understanding

If pairwise work is O(n²), what happens when n triples?

Reveal the explanation

The leading quadratic work grows by a factor of nine. Fixed overhead and other terms may make measured time differ.

An operating model for algorithms, complexity & data structures

Complexity is a way to eliminate impossible designs before implementation. It does not replace profiling. A quadratic algorithm can be ideal at small scale, and an asymptotically elegant method can lose because it creates scattered memory access or expensive setup. The right procedure is to estimate growth, then measure the actual operating range.

The gotcha. A clean workflow diagram describes dependency order. It does not prove that any boundary is correct; each transition needs its own observable acceptance test.

Worked system: why attention makes sequence length expensive

A standard attention layer compares each token with every other token. At sequence length n, the score matrix has n² entries. Doubling a prompt from 4,000 to 8,000 tokens creates four times as many pairwise scores; it does not merely add another 4,000 operations. The same pattern appears in all-pairs similarity search, dense graph algorithms, and naive duplicate detection. Complexity tells you which axis will dominate before a profiler can.

But asymptotic notation is only the beginning. An implementation that never materializes the full score matrix can change memory behavior radically while preserving the mathematical result. A hash index can turn a scan into an expected constant-time lookup while introducing build cost and collisions. A practical design asks two questions together: what grows fastest as the input changes, and what does one unit of that work mean in bytes, cache misses, network round trips, or kernel launches on the actual machine?

Notebook: Trace a byte budget

Write one back-of-the-envelope calculation for every large intermediate. Count elements, bytes per element, and operations. If either number is outside the target machine’s capacity, change the algorithm before optimizing code.

items = 1_000_000
bytes_per_item = 4
working_set = items * bytes_per_item
print(f"{working_set / 2**20:.1f} MiB")
# Now include every copy, index, and temporary buffer.
What to test next. 1. Define input scale: Count records, edges, dimensions, and sequence length. 2. Choose representation: Use an array, index, graph, cache, or stream. 3. Find dependencies: Separate parallel work from reductions and sequential state. 4. Measure reality: Include allocation, locality, I/O, and constants.

The gotcha. A small inspection script proves only the quantities it prints. Preserve units, shapes, versions, and the input fixture beside its output.

A rigorous way to practice

  1. Define input scale. Count records, edges, dimensions, and sequence length.
  2. Choose representation. Use an array, index, graph, cache, or stream.
  3. Find dependencies. Separate parallel work from reductions and sequential state.
  4. Measure reality. Include allocation, locality, I/O, and constants.

Write one back-of-the-envelope calculation for every large intermediate. Count elements, bytes per element, and operations. If either number is outside the target machine’s capacity, change the algorithm before optimizing code.

The gotcha. Passing each component check separately does not prove the composed path preserves identity, units, ordering, or authority.

Growth covers work, space, communication, and span

Complexity rules out impossible designs before profiling. Work counts operations; span counts the longest dependency chain; communication counts bytes, messages, and synchronization rounds.

  • Worst-case bounds protect tail behavior. Good average performance can coexist with an adversarial outage.
  • Amortized analysis prices a sequence. Occasional resizing can still yield constant average append cost.
  • Lower bounds expose changed assumptions. Beating a general bound usually changes keys, error tolerance, preprocessing, or the query.

The gotcha. Big-O hides constants and units; calculate bytes or operations at the intended scale.

Data structures purchase operations with layout

  • Arrays favor indexed scans and locality. Middle insertion requires movement.
  • Hash tables favor exact lookup. They spend ordering and collision management.
  • Trees preserve ordered operations. Balance maintains logarithmic depth.
  • Graph storage follows density. Adjacency lists cost O(V+E); matrices cost O(V²).
  • Indexes trade build cost for queries. Approximate indexes also trade recall for speed.

The gotcha. A lookup bound ignores iteration, cache misses, serialization, and operation mix.

AI complexity starts with named tensor axes

  • Dense attention couples positions quadratically. Doubling length creates four times the pairwise scores.
  • Autoregressive decoding retains a serial dependency. Batching adds parallel work across requests.
  • Retrieval separates recall from ranking. A fast index supplies candidates; a slower model reranks a bounded set.
  • Checkpointing trades arithmetic for memory. Recomputed activations reduce stored state.

The gotcha. A faster kernel changes nothing when queues, transfers, retrieval, or tokenization dominate.
